text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The leading government party the Coalition party will not rescind the cooperation agreement with the Centre Party as an ultimatum from the Reform Party demands, Vaehi said.
- Finnish Culture Minister Claes Andersson paid a visit to Tallinn, opening an exhibition on Finnish media art.
- Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjorn Jagland arrives for a visit and will meet the Estonian president, prime minister and parliament members.
- The Estonian National Culture Fund will spend 3.9 million on grants and stipends this year.
- The small Progressive Party and the Farmers Assembly, both with 500 members, will sign an association agreement on Wednesday, planning a full merger in six months.
- The sum of the firms unpaid social tax has reached 1.3 billion kroons, leader of the Social Insurance Department said.
- Parliamentary commission on the SIA tape affair, which brought down the previouis government, proposed that the government improve legislation on secret surveillance.
- There is no government crisis but only a Reform Party pose and early elections of parliament are unlikely, Centre Party leader Edgar Savisaar says in an interview.
- Reform Party secretary general Heiki Kranich predicts in an interview that the current coalition will split up.
